stage.note: an enhancement STAGE: it restores/upscales another stage's output (or an upload); it generates nothing from text and takes no prompt

cannot.what: take a text prompt: SeedVR2Conditioning supplies fixed positive/negative embeddings from the checkpoint (reference code ships pos_emb.pt/neg_emb.pt); any CLIPTextEncode in the graph is unused
be robust to heavy degradations and very large motions (official: 'sometimes not robust ... fail to fully remove the degradation or simply generate unpleasing details')
leave clean sources alone: 'tend to overly generate details on inputs with very light degradations, e.g., 720p AIGC videos, leading to oversharpened results occasionally'
load GGUF or the numz-named files (seedvr2_ema_*, models/SEEDVR2/) through the native nodes: GGUF stays a custom-node feature (maintainer statement)
load the original ByteDance .pth weights: the native nodes read the Comfy-Org conversion (seedvr2_convert.py)
multi-step sampling as a documented option: the model is one-step; the templates fix steps 1 / cfg 1 and other values are NOT FOUND in official text

params.name: scale
params.meaning: the upscale factor applied BEFORE the DiT: SeedVR2 restores at the resolution it is handed
params.interactions: VRAM and time scale with output megapixels x frames (see the chunk-size law); very large stills: docs suggest downscaling to ~0.35 Mpx with ImageScaleToTotalPixels before upscaling; lower the multiplier on clean sources to limit oversharpening

params.name: steps / cfg / denoise
params.meaning: one-step model: steps 1, cfg 1 (negative conditioning is a fixed embedding), denoise 1 = 'full restore'
params.interactions: the templates fix steps and cfg and only expose denoise; other values: NOT FOUND officially

params.name: sampler_name / scheduler
params.interactions: no official guidance beyond the defaults

params.name: seed
params.meaning: a one-step model still consumes noise; the seed changes micro-detail

params.name: color_correction_method
params.meaning: match the output's colours to the resized original: lab = CIELAB transfer 'most faithful'; wavelet = low-frequency colour only; adain = per-channel mean/std 'fastest, global tint'; none = geometry alignment only
params.interactions: lab needs the most memory (constants: per-frame byte multipliers LAB 13, wavelet 10, adain 6; chunked with OOM back-off)

params.name: VAE tiling
params.meaning: spatial/temporal tiling of the causal 3D VAE
params.interactions: ComfyUI's VAE wrapper also auto-dispatches tiling from free VRAM (PR #14424); tiled decode tile 32-96 latent units (<=768 px)

params.name: chunking_mode / frames_per_chunk
params.meaning: auto = 'predict the largest chunk that fits free VRAM' (the law below); manual = frames_per_chunk exactly (4n+1, default 21)
params.interactions: the KSampler runs once per chunk; SeedVR2TemporalMerge recombines

params.name: temporal_overlap (chunks)
params.meaning: latent frames shared by adjacent chunks, Hann-crossfaded by SeedVR2TemporalMerge
params.interactions: 0 = hard cut at chunk borders; clamped to chunk_latent-1; raise it to hide seams

params.name: VRAM chunk-size law
params.meaning: official: 'the sampler's activation wall is linear in T_latent * pixel area' - max_latent_frames = (free_GiB - RESERVED - K*SIGMA) / (GIB_PER_MPX_FRAME * megapixels)

defaults.fitted_on: 3B fp16, RTX 5090, 17-cell resolution sweep + T bisection

params.interactions: max_latent_frames = (free_GiB - 8.5 - 4*0.55) / (0.55 * output_megapixels); pixel frames = 4*latent_frames - 3. Example (3B fp16, RTX 5090): 1920x1080 output = 2.07 Mpx -> 1.14 GiB per latent frame; 24 GiB free -> ~11 latent frames ~ 41 pixel frames per chunk; latent frames = (pixel_frames - 1) / 4 + 1; pixel-frame temporal downsample 4, spatial 8, 16 latent channels

params.name: frame count
params.meaning: pads frames to 4n+1 (1 passes; 2-4 padded to 5) by repeating the last frame; SeedVR2PostProcessing crops back
params.interactions: manual frames_per_chunk must itself be 4n+1 (node step 4)

params.name: weight_dtype
params.meaning: the templates load the pre-quantised int8_convrot files with 'default'
params.interactions: pick precision by FILE (fp16 / fp8_e4m3fn / int8_convrot / mxfp8 / nvfp4), not by re-casting

rules.message: SeedVR2 encodes/decodes with its own causal 3D VAE (seedvr2_ema_vae_fp16.safetensors == ema_vae_fp16.safetensors, 16-channel); every official template loads it, no other VAE fits the 5-D latent

the native loader takes the Comfy-Org repack files in models/diffusion_models (seedvr2_{3b,7b,7b_sharp}_{fp16,fp8_e4m3fn,int8_convrot,mxfp8,nvfp4}.safetensors); numz-named files (seedvr2_ema_*, models/SEEDVR2), GGUF and the ByteDance .pth are not loadable natively

the official templates load the pre-quantised int8/fp8 SeedVR2 files with weight_dtype 'default'; precision is chosen by file (fp16 / fp8_e4m3fn / int8_convrot / mxfp8 / nvfp4 pairs of the same size), not by re-casting an already quantised file
SeedVR2 has no text encoder: KSampler's positive/negative must come from SeedVR2Conditioning (model + the VAE-encoded latent); CLIPTextEncode conditioning is wrong for this model
the frames must pass SeedVR2Preprocess before VAE encoding (drops alpha, clamps 0-1, pads H/W to multiples of 16 and frames to 4n+1); SeedVR2Conditioning requires the resulting 5-D latent

SeedVR2PostProcessing must follow the decode, with original_resized_images = the RESIZED input (the same tensor fed to SeedVR2Preprocess, not the raw LoadImage): it crops the padding back, re-applies alpha and does the optional colour match
SeedVR2 is a one-step model ('One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training'); every official template fixes steps=1 and values other than 1 are not documented
cfg 1 in every official template: the negative conditioning is a fixed embedding, guidance above 1 is undocumented

Split SeedVR2 Latent emits a LIST of chunks: the sampler runs per chunk and Merge SeedVR2 Latents must recombine them, with its temporal_overlap wired from the Chunk node's temporal_overlap output (the effective overlap after clamping) before VAEDecodeTiled

when chunking, the chunk list feeds BOTH SeedVR2Conditioning.vae_conditioning and KSampler.latent_image (node description), otherwise the conditioning latent and the sampled latent have different lengths
frames_per_chunk is pixel frames and must be 4n+1 (1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21 ...); the node steps by 4 from 1 and the VAE's temporal downsample is 4

official chunk-size law (comfy/ldm/seedvr/constants.py): a clip whose latent frames x output megapixels exceeds (free_GiB - 10.7) / 0.55 will not sample in one latent - e.g. 24 GiB free fits ~11 latent frames (~41 pixel frames) at 1080p output, ~5 (~17 frames) at 4K. Use the -chunked recipe (auto applies this law), lower the scale, or trim. The 7B needs more: NOT FOUND

SeedVR2 restores frames, it does not add or drop them: CreateVideo.fps must be the source fps wired from GetVideoComponents (the template links fps, audio and bit_depth through); a literal fps changes playback speed
a CLIPTextEncode in a SeedVR2 graph is dead weight: the model takes no prompt, SeedVR2Conditioning supplies the fixed embeddings
native SeedVR2 nodes exist from ComfyUI v0.28.0 (templates: minComfyUIVersion 0.28.0); the pinned 0.35.0 image qualifies

prompting.note: not applicable: SeedVR2 takes no text prompt in ComfyUI. SeedVR2Conditioning supplies fixed positive/negative embeddings stored in the converted checkpoint (reference implementation ships pos_emb.pt / neg_emb.pt).

pitfalls.cause: attention backend, precision or an incomplete download (official docs troubleshooting)
pitfalls.fix: 'Disable FlashAttention, switch to FP16/FP8, verify complete file downloads, or disable live preview'

pitfalls.symptom: out of memory on a clip
pitfalls.cause: latent frames x output megapixels over the chunk-size law
pitfalls.fix: the -chunked recipe (SeedVR2TemporalChunk auto), a smaller scale, or trim and process segments (template tip); add chunk temporal_overlap to hide seams

pitfalls.symptom: oversharpened, invented texture on a clean or AIGC 720p source
pitfalls.cause: official limitation: 'overly generate details on inputs with very light degradations'
pitfalls.fix: lower the scale multiplier, prefer 3B/7B over 7B-sharp; (numz only) small input_noise_scale / latent_noise_scale 0.01-0.05

pitfalls.symptom: degradation not removed / unpleasing details on heavy degradation or big motion
pitfalls.fix: no fix beyond pre-denoising; expect it

pitfalls.cause: native nodes read models/diffusion_models + models/vae (Comfy-Org repack names); numz reads models/SEEDVR2 with seedvr2_ema_* names; ByteDance .pth are unconverted
pitfalls.fix: use the Comfy-Org files in profile.files

pitfalls.cause: original_resized_images wired from the raw LoadImage instead of the resized RGBA
pitfalls.fix: JoinImageWithAlpha -> resize -> feed the SAME resized tensor to SeedVR2Preprocess and to SeedVR2PostProcessing.original_resized_images (the recipe does)

pitfalls.symptom: frame count differs from the input mid-graph
pitfalls.cause: SeedVR2Preprocess pads to 4n+1 by repeating the last frame
pitfalls.fix: nothing: SeedVR2PostProcessing crops back to the reference length
the numz pack (community_alternatives): GGUF Q4_K_M + BlockSwap + VAE tiling on <=8 GB; 4n+1 batch_size

pitfalls.symptom: VRAM tripled after a PyTorch upgrade (numz pack)
pitfalls.fix: update the pack (2.5.23 extended the workaround)

pitfalls.cause: a single search summary claims '7B FP16 for quality, 3B FP8 for speed, avoid 7B FP8' - unverified
pitfalls.fix: the official templates ship INT8 for both sizes; start there
